major_work.title: EXP-E-005 Liquidity Vacuum vs Demand Surge falsification audit
major_work.summary: The challenger is directionally useful and correctly abstains from hidden-actor intent, but its mechanism labels are not yet operationally identifiable. Trade/quote snapshots can describe impact, spread and displayed depth, but cannot by themselves establish whether a move was caused by durable demand expansion versus offer withdrawal/cancellation/hidden-liquidity dynamics. A reproducible label protocol and event-level order lifecycle evidence are required before treating DEMAND_SURGE_SUPPORTED or LIQUIDITY_VACUUM_SUPPORTED as validation targets.

findings.finding: The proposed target states risk becoming circular labels derived from the same features later used to predict them. Without an independent labeling rule or external ground truth, a model can appear accurate by reproducing its own heuristic definition rather than validating a market mechanism.
findings.required_fix: AI-C must define label construction independently from evaluated features, report inter-rater/algorithmic reliability, and distinguish descriptive state classification from causal mechanism identification.

findings.finding: Authoritative tick and quote snapshots are insufficient if they do not preserve order-event lifecycle. Displayed depth disappearance can reflect execution, cancellation, repricing, feed aggregation, hidden/iceberg liquidity, auction transitions or venue fragmentation.
findings.required_fix: Require event-level provenance where available: exchange/venue scope, sequence/timestamp alignment, add/modify/cancel/execute semantics, auction/VI/halt flags, and explicit UNKNOWN when lifecycle attribution is unavailable.

findings.finding: Open/close auctions, volatility interruption, halts, disclosure/news timestamps and cross-venue fragmentation can create apparent vacuum/surge signatures unrelated to the hypothesized continuous-market mechanism.
findings.required_fix: Pre-register exclusion/segmentation rules and compare clean continuous-session samples with contaminated samples rather than pooling them.

findings.finding: Even with event-level order data, observed order-flow mechanics do not identify a hidden actor's motive. The existing safety contract is correct and must remain a hard production guard.
findings.required_fix: Use descriptive wording such as 'observed aggressive-flow dominance' or 'displayed-offer depletion pattern'; do not promote to actor intent, accumulation/distribution or manipulation.

small_works.detail: Point-in-time feature contract, UNKNOWN abstention, no-production-probability gate and hidden-actor safety language are appropriate and should be preserved.
Known SELF-HEAL L1/L2 and Ultra-Parallel V2 closure fingerprints were not re-investigated because this run found no new evidence packet changing those prior findings.

handoffs.task: Operationalize EXP-E-005 labels without feature-label circularity; add independent label protocol, reliability, event-lifecycle provenance, contamination splits, and walk-forward validation.
Revise EXP-E-005 architecture to separate descriptive microstructure state from causal mechanism claims and make order-lifecycle provenance a capability gate.

Only if EXP-E-005 proceeds to data validation, expose venue/scope/timestamp/sequence/add-modify-cancel-execute/auction-VI-halt provenance; do not build a new tick pipeline before validation demand is confirmed.

next_work: Audit the next new P0/P1 or AI-B required-review evidence packet; do not repeat EXP-E-005 unless its fingerprint/evidence changes.
